newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500 futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500 futures finish higher.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended higher after a quiet session spent watching T-bonds and waiting for new fundamental impetus.
March Standard and Poor's 500 futures rallied back into positive territory after Treasury bond futures closed, recovering from an earlier lethargic tone.
March posted a session high at 814.80 after the March T-bond closed up from its low on a flurry of late short-covering. S&Ps later surpassed that high to reach 815.00.
"The bond close gave us some relief," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
She noted buy stops in March S&Ps at 810.00 and 812.00 that pushed the contract to 814.80. Locals were the best buyers on that bounce, with dealer participation only light, she said.
Technical momentum heading into the close kept the tone buoyant, but for the most part March S&Ps were still range-bound waiting for the week's news to unfurl, floor traders said.
"Everybody was a little wary," another S&P 500 trader said. He characterized the day's trade as uninspired but resilient.
At midday, March S&Ps had downticked with T-bonds after results of the U.S. Treasury's two-year note auction.
Treasury sold $17.5 billion in two-year notes at 5.885 percent high yield, with 94 percent awarded at the high.
The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.21 times with non-competitive bids of $1.321 billion.
With the two-year out of the way, traders were looking ahead to the five-year auction and the first leg of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
The Redbook Retail Sales Index, up 2.5 percent in February, had scant impact on the market, traders said.
One trader pegged support for Wednesday at 810.00 and resistance at 815.60.

March S&P 500s closed up 1.60 pts to 814.15, Value Lines rose 1.40 to 719.50, Midcap firmed 1.55 to 268.35, NYSE Composite rose 0.65 to 426.55, Nasdaq 100 fell 2.00 to 884.50, and Nikkei rose 330.0 to 19,170.0. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
